title: Composition of normalized ordinary derived root comparisons
statement: Let ell be prime and T a scheme. For natural numbers n ≤ m ≤ r, let a,b,c be CoefficientLineComparison records, as defined by def-pur-finite-smooth-coefficient-arrows, for the coefficient quotient maps A_r→A_m, A_m→A_n, A_r→A_n, respectively, where A_i=ULift (ULift (ZMod (ell^i))) and the root orders are ell^r,ell^m,ell^n. Then ordinaryScalar(A_m→A_n) applied to a.derivedIso.hom, followed by b.derivedIso.hom, equals the canonical ordinaryAssociator component on the degree-zero ell^r Tate line, followed by c.derivedIso.hom. No positivity of the indices, smoothness or geometric invertibility hypothesis is required.

source.place: Part (3), orientation: composition of the power maps of roots, generator normalization and exact single-object scalar comparison.

proof.text: Compose the root maps with the monic inclusion of the target root kernel into G_m. The roots_power equations reduce the comparison to multiplication of the exponents ell^(r-m) and ell^(m-n), including equal indices. Transpose the ordinary scalar-extension maps to maps from the Tate line into scalar restrictions. The lineHomEquiv universal property detects them on generators; generators and the root equality give the insertion composition law.

Rewrite the three derived comparison maps using their proved exact scalar-insertion normalization. Apply the composition law for exact degree-zero scalar insertions to the generator-detected ordinary insertion equation. The coefficient quotient maps compose by the unique ZMod ring homomorphism, lifted twice. Their canonical scalar associator is precisely the left-adjoint composition comparison in that insertion law. All steps are proved in Lean.

from.place: Proof through finite reduction compatibilities (3): exact degree-zero scalar normalization of the rank-one root comparison.

lean.statement:
theorem ordinaryRootDerivedComp
    (ell : ℕ) [Fact ell.Prime] (T : Scheme.{u})
    {r m n : ℕ} (hmr : m ≤ r) (hnm : n ≤ m)
    (a : CoefficientLineComparison (FiniteReduction.quotient ell hmr)
      (ell ^ r) (ell ^ m) (CharP.cast_eq_zero _ _) (CharP.cast_eq_zero _ _) T)
    (b : CoefficientLineComparison (FiniteReduction.quotient ell hnm)
      (ell ^ m) (ell ^ n) (CharP.cast_eq_zero _ _) (CharP.cast_eq_zero _ _) T)
    (c : CoefficientLineComparison (FiniteReduction.quotient ell (hnm.trans hmr))
      (ell ^ r) (ell ^ n) (CharP.cast_eq_zero _ _) (CharP.cast_eq_zero _ _) T) :
    (ordinaryScalar (FiniteReduction.quotient ell hnm) T).map a.derivedIso.hom ≫
      b.derivedIso.hom =
    (ordinaryAssociator T ell hmr hnm).hom.app
      (ordinaryFiniteLine (coefficient ell r) (ell ^ r) (CharP.cast_eq_zero _ _) T) ≫
      c.derivedIso.hom
